before.title: ABS/HECU Brake-Fluid Leak Causing Electrical Short and Engine-Bay Fire
before.description: Brake fluid can leak internally inside the Hydraulic Electronic Control Unit (HECU) of the anti-lock brake system, causing an electrical short that can ignite an engine-compartment fire even while parked and off. Kia advised owners to park outside and away from structures until repaired. On the first-generation Forte this is covered by NHTSA recall 21V331. This is a fire risk independent of the engine recalls.
before.solution: Under safety recall 21V331, dealers inspect the HECU for leaking brake fluid, replace the HECU if leaking, and install a new multi-fuse (30A instead of 40A) in the HECU circuit to prevent an over-current condition, free of charge. Out of warranty, a leaking HECU/ABS module is replaced and the brake system bled.

proposal.title: ABS/HECU Brake-Fluid Leak Causing Electrical Short and Engine-Bay Fire
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 23V652000 (Kia SC284) covers certain 2010-2013 Forte and Forte Koup vehicles equipped with Electronic Stability Control. The Hydraulic Electronic Control Unit (HECU) may experience an electrical short that can cause an engine-compartment fire while the vehicle is parked or being driven. Kia and NHTSA advise affected owners to park outdoors and away from structures until the recall is completed.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for recall 23V652000. A Kia dealer installs new lower-amperage fuse or fuses to prevent an overcurrent condition in the HECU circuit, free of charge. This proposal does not recommend a retail HECU or fuse because the campaign remedy is VIN-specific and dealer-installed. If the ABS or malfunction light illuminates, or there is a burning smell or smoke, stop safely, turn the engine off and arrange towing to a Kia dealer.

before.title: Airbag Control Unit Electrical Fault - Airbags May Not Deploy in a Crash
before.description: The Airbag Control Unit (ACU) can suffer an internal electrical fault. On 2010-2013 cars the ACU's ASIC chip is susceptible to electrical overstress during a frontal crash (recall SC165 / 18V363), and on 2017-2018 cars the ACU cover can contact and damage a circuit-board chip (recall SC226). Either fault can deactivate the frontal airbags and seatbelt pretensioners so they fail to deploy in a collision.
before.solution: Dealers inspect and reprogram or replace the airbag control unit under the applicable recall at no charge. Owners of affected earlier models were also eligible for reimbursement/compensation under the related class-action settlement.
symptoms: Airbags fail to deploy in a crash

proposal.title: Airbag Control Unit Electrical Fault - Airbags May Not Deploy in a Crash
proposal.description: Two Kia safety recalls match this page’s retained year groups. Under 18V363000 (SC165), the airbag control unit in certain 2010-2013 Forte vehicles can suffer electrical overstress during a frontal crash, preventing the frontal airbags and seatbelt pretensioners from deploying. Under 22V031000 (SC226), the ACU cover in certain 2017-2018 Forte vehicles can contact a memory chip, illuminate the airbag warning light with DTC B1620 and deactivate the airbags.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for both recalls. For 18V363000, Kia installs an extension wire-harness kit between the ACU and vehicle harness. For 22V031000, Kia updates ACU software when B1620 is absent and replaces the ACU when B1620 is present. Both remedies are free and VIN-specific. No retail airbag-control part should be purchased from this page. If the airbag warning light stays on, follow Kia’s recall instructions and arrange dealer diagnosis.
symptoms: DTC B1620 on later recall population
Airbags or pretensioners may not deploy in a crash

before.title: Clear-Coat / Paint Peeling and Flaking (Snow White Pearl and Light Colors)
before.description: The factory clear coat delaminates and peels away in sheets, most commonly on Snow White Pearl / Clear White and other light colors and on horizontal panels (hood, roof, trunk) plus mirrors and door handles. Owners attribute it to a too-thin clear coat with inadequate UV protection; a paint chip lets water wick under the clear coat, which then spreads. Kia customer service has acknowledged the issue on 2011-2014 cars; sometimes covered as goodwill despite no formal recall.
before.solution: Affected panels must be sanded and repainted/re-cleared; whole-car respray in severe cases. Some owners obtain partial or full goodwill assistance from Kia depending on VIN, paint code, and mileage; filing an NHTSA complaint helps document the defect.
symptoms: Bare/faded paint on hood and roof

before.title: Connecting Rod Bearing Failure Causing Engine Seizure, Sudden Stall and Fire Risk
before.description: Excessive connecting rod bearing wear on the Theta II and Nu engines can cause the engine to knock, seize, and stall without warning while driving, with a documented risk of an engine-compartment fire. This is the failure mode behind the NHTSA/Kia KSDS recall and the Hyundai-Kia engine class settlement, distinct from routine oil-consumption knock. Owners report catastrophic bottom-end failure, metal in the oil, and no-restart. Root cause is manufacturing debris left in the crankcase restricting oil flow to the rod bearings.
before.solution: Kia dealers apply the Knock Sensor Detection System (KSDS) ECU software update that triggers limp mode (DTC P1326) before catastrophic failure, inspect for oil/fuel leaks, and replace the long-block/short-block if bearing damage is found. Repairs are warranted 15 years/150,000 miles under the KSDS campaign and covered by the engine class-action settlement (reimbursement for prior repairs).
symptoms: Sudden engine stall or seizure while driving
Engine warning light and limp mode (P1326)

before.title: CVT Shudder and Hesitation Under Acceleration
before.description: The IVT (Intelligent Variable Transmission, Kia's name for their CVT) in the 2019-2024 Forte develops a shuddering sensation during light-to-moderate acceleration, particularly from stops and at speeds between 20-45 mph. The issue is caused by the CVT chain and pulley interface wearing irregularly. Kia has released multiple software updates to improve shift mapping and reduce the shudder sensation.
before.solution: Have dealer perform TCU software update (latest calibration). If shudder persists after software update, CVT fluid change with genuine Kia CVTF may help. In severe cases, CVT valve body or complete CVT replacement under powertrain warranty (10 years/100,000 miles). Kia part #45280-2F100 for CVT fluid.
symptoms: Hesitation or rubber-band feel during acceleration
Vibration felt through accelerator pedal at 20-45 mph
Whining noise from transmission during acceleration
RPMs fluctuate unexpectedly during steady cruise

citations.title: KiaForums.com - 2019+ Forte IVT shudder discussion (200+ replies)

communityRecommendations.content: Start with the free TCU software update at the dealer - this resolves or significantly improves the shudder in about 60% of cases

before.title: Nu 2.0L GDI Engine Knocking and Oil Consumption
before.description: The 2nd generation Forte with the Nu 2.0L GDI engine (2014-2018) can develop engine knocking and excessive oil consumption. Similar to the Theta II issues but in the Nu engine family, piston ring wear leads to oil blow-by and cylinder scoring. Kia extended warranty coverage under the engine campaign. Affected engines may consume 1+ quart of oil per 1,000 miles.
before.solution: Contact dealer for engine campaign eligibility check. Dealer will perform oil consumption test (requires multiple visits over 1,000 miles). If consumption exceeds Kia threshold (1 qt per 1,000 miles), engine replacement or piston ring replacement is performed under warranty extension. Keep all oil purchase and change receipts.
symptoms: Engine knocking at idle and under load
Excessive oil consumption (1+ qt per 1,000 miles)
Blue or white smoke from exhaust
Check engine light with misfire codes

before.title: Front Strut Bearing and Upper Spring Pad Noise/Failure
before.description: The 3rd generation Forte (2019-2024) develops a creaking, popping, or groaning noise from the front suspension when turning the steering wheel, particularly at low speeds and over bumps. The front strut bearing and upper spring pad deteriorate prematurely. Kia issued a TSB to replace both components with updated parts. The issue is especially prevalent in colder climates.
before.solution: Have dealer check for Kia TSB addressing front strut bearing and upper spring pad replacement on 2019-2024 Forte. Replacement of both strut mount bearings and upper spring pads ($50-80 per side in parts). Labor is approximately 1.5-2 hours per side. Some owners combine with strut replacement for a more complete refresh.
symptoms: Creaking or groaning noise when turning steering wheel
Popping sound over bumps from front suspension
Noise most noticeable at low speeds and during parking
Sound more pronounced in cold weather
Steering feels rough when turning slowly

proposal.title: Front Strut Bearing and Upper Spring Pad Noise/Failure
proposal.description: Kia bulletin CHA121 applies to certain 2019-2024 Forte vehicles and documents an intermittent front-suspension noise while turning the steering wheel, whether the vehicle is moving or stationary. Kia’s procedure replaces the front strut bearing and upper spring pad on both front strut assemblies. The bulletin describes a noise repair, not a safety recall or proof of complete strut failure.
proposal.solution: Ask a Kia dealer or qualified suspension shop to confirm bulletin CHA121 applies and to inspect both front strut assemblies. The bulletin replaces both front strut bearings and upper spring pads and requires new locking nuts during reassembly. This proposal does not recommend a retail part because the repair is production- and fitment-specific and requires strut disassembly, correct torque and verification after repair.
symptoms: Intermittent front suspension noise while turning
Noise while steering when moving or stationary

before.title: Headlight and Taillight Moisture Condensation
before.description: The 2019-2023 Forte commonly develops condensation (fogging) inside the headlight and taillight assemblies. Water enters through degraded seals or vent tubes that become clogged. In severe cases, standing water can short out LED driver boards or corrode wiring connectors. Kia has replaced headlight assemblies under warranty for many owners, though the issue can return if the seal design is not updated.
before.solution: If under warranty, have dealer replace headlight assembly with updated seal design. Aftermarket fix: remove headlight assembly, dry thoroughly, reseal with Permatex Ultra Grey RTV silicone (#82195), and ensure vent tubes are clear. For LED taillights with condensation, replacement is usually needed ($200-400 per side).
symptoms: Visible moisture or fogging inside headlight lenses
Water pooling at bottom of headlight housing
Reduced headlight brightness due to fogging

before.title: Motor-Driven Power Steering (MDPS) Flexible Coupler Knocking/Clunking
before.description: The star-shaped rubber flexible coupler inside the electric power-steering (MDPS) motor wears prematurely, producing a distinct click, clunk, or knock felt through the steering wheel and column when turning, going over bumps, or maneuvering at low speed. Kia acknowledged the premature coupler wear in a TSB; unlike some other Kia models the coupler fix was not applied to the Forte, so many owners pay out of pocket.
before.solution: Replace the flexible coupler (rubber/spline joint) in the MDPS unit; labor requires accessing the steering column/motor. On 2014-2018 models a Steering Angle Sensor (SAS) calibration is required afterward. In some cases the full MDPS column assembly is replaced.
symptoms: Noise over bumps felt in the column

before.title: Premature Low-Beam Headlight Burnout from Melting Connector/Socket
before.description: Owners repeatedly replace low-beam headlight bulbs, sometimes multiple times in a year. The root cause is frequently a failing headlamp socket/pigtail connector that overheats and melts (a high-resistance/loose-connection condition), rather than defective bulbs. Kia issued campaign SC149/SC149R1 covering the connector on certain VINs. Distinct from lens moisture condensation.
before.solution: Replace the melted headlamp socket/pigtail connector and repair the affected wiring, then fit a quality bulb; verify supply voltage and ground integrity. Persistent cases require harness/connector replacement rather than repeated bulb swaps. Covered free on qualifying VINs under SC149.
